clue.text: Leading male with dad bod

parts.note: a dad is a father
bod is short for body, and a body is a figure

explanation.surface: A lead actor who sports a soft, paunchy 'dad bod' physique.
explanation.definitionFit: A father figure is an older man others look up to and follow, a guiding male role model.

clue.text: One dropping pound, picked up and pocketed by smoker

indicators.note: being pocketed by something means going inside it

parts.note: a fumer is one who fumes or gives off smoke

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts the letters so they read bottom to top

parts.note: LB is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: A smoker drops a pound coin, picks it up and slips it into a pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A fumbler is someone who drops or mishandles things, such as a catch.

clue.text: Spectator going up to support opener in the Ashes?

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means standing underneath the other piece
the opener in a word is its first letter
in a down clue, going up means the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: a seer is one who sees, an onlooker

explanation.surface: A cricket fan climbing up to back the opening batsman in the Ashes series.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the England-Australia cricket series, and an opener is the batsman who starts the innings; here the Ashes are ash trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashes are examples of trees, so the question mark marks a definition by example.

clue.text: Catch second name after nurse runs into empty ambulance

indicators.note: the second and name follow the nurse

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse

indicators.note: the runs go into the shell of the ambulance
an empty word keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters give AE
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A nurse dashes to an empty ambulance just after being named second.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare is to trap or capture, as in a snare.

clue.text: See 1
Be left at home with husband, flipping bore

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: flipping turns the word for bore over so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: to tire someone is to bore them

explanation.surface: Someone left at home with a dull husband grumbles about the flipping bore.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to receive something bequeathed in a will, to be left it.

clue.text: Labour wants to lose bankers with redistribution for capital

indicators.note: redistributing shares the letters out in a new order
the bankers are the letters at each edge of the word, which are dropped

parts.note: without its ends this leaves ANT

explanation.surface: The Labour Party wants to curb the bankers and redistribute capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the outer letters of 'wants' leaves ANT, which is shuffled with LABOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulan Bator is the capital city of Mongolia.

clue.text: Increase tax in confused battle, member must go

indicators.note: the tax sits inside the remaining letters
the member must leave the word for a confused battle

parts.note: a melee is a confused, disorderly fight
M is the abbreviation for member, as in MP
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A government raises tax in the middle of a messy political fight, and one member has to resign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' looks like an anagram signal, but it belongs with 'battle' as a single definition of a disorderly fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate is to raise or lift something higher.

clue.text: Make love with fellow, American idiot

parts.note: do can mean make, as in do a meal
O is love, nil in tennis

explanation.surface: A crude remark about a foolish American man who wants to make love.
explanation.definitionFit: Doofus is American slang for a stupid or foolish person.

clue.text: Element of surprise, initially therein a memoir isn't true

indicators.note: letters that are not true are out of their proper order
initially takes the first letter

parts.note: first letter S
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A memoir has a twist: its element of surprise is that it is not really true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Element of surprise' is a stock phrase; only 'Element' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An immersion heater is an electric heating element placed in a water tank.

clue.text: State two answers when tackling Latin question

indicators.note: the two letters grab hold of the others between them

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer, so two give A and A
to ask is to question

explanation.surface: A pupil gives two answers when faced with a question in Latin class.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is the largest US state.

clue.text: Old relation in favour of European support

parts.note: for means in favour of
to bear is to support a weight

explanation.surface: An elderly relative backs European support.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is an ancestor, a relative from earlier generations.

clue.text: Cuts uncertainty in wagers

indicators.note: the uncertainty sits inside the wagers

parts.note: bets are wagers
risk is uncertainty about an outcome

explanation.surface: Budget cuts create uncertainty in the betting market.
explanation.definitionFit: Briskets are cuts of beef from the breast of the animal.

clue.text: One doing sport to take off short top

indicators.note: short means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: to skip off is to take off, leave in a hurry
a jumper is a knitted top, a sweater

explanation.surface: An athlete is told to remove a cropped top before competing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' suggests the jump itself, but it gives the word for a hasty exit; a jumper is British for a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski jumper competes in the winter sport of ski jumping.

clue.text: Called in time to get sex? Did escort?

parts.note: it is slang for sex
led means guided or escorted

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about whether a call-in date ended in sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Titled means named, given a title, as a book is called something.

clue.text: Cool morning, rejected air conditioning for fan

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: On a cool morning someone turns down the air conditioning in favour of a fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fan' looks like a cooling device to pair with the air conditioning; it means an enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: A maniac can be an obsessive enthusiast, as in a football maniac.

clue.text: Score from area? Right to practise shooting here?

parts.note: a range is where people practise shooting

explanation.surface: A footballer scores from the area, then wonders whether to practise shooting on a range.
explanation.definitionFit: To score music is to arrange it for instruments.

clue.text: Tweet letter: pleased Tom might do this in retirement

parts.note: chi is a Greek letter

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a contented tomcat purrs

explanation.surface: Someone tweets a happy message about their cat, Tom, enjoying retirement.
explanation.definitionFit: A chirrup is a bird's chirping call, a tweet.

clue.text: One next to Carol, not caught messing about in school photo

indicators.note: the other letters go inside the school

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

indicators.note: the one goes beside the jumbled letters
messing about jumbles the letters
not drops the letter for caught

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pupil sitting next to Carol fools around and spoils the school photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' seems to set the scene of a class photo, but here it means a group of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: A Polaroid is an instant photograph from the camera of that brand.

clue.text: Couch potato originally to share nuts

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter

parts.note: first letter P

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A couch potato is told to share the nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couch potato' reads as one phrase, but 'Couch' is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To couch something is to express it in particular words, to word it.

clue.text: Towards the end, accepting work to feed the kids?

indicators.note: accepting takes the work inside

parts.note: late means near the end of a period
an act is a deed or piece of work

explanation.surface: Near the end of the day someone takes on work to feed their children.
explanation.definitionFit: To lactate is to produce milk, as a mother does to nourish young; kids are also young goats.

clue.text: Called upon second couple to bonk: video shot

indicators.note: shot means wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the second pair of letters in bonk
taken as written

explanation.surface: A racy video is filmed of a second couple having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: To invoke is to call on someone, a deity or authority, for help.

clue.text: Person raking in money in dock after court briefly disrupted

indicators.note: the dock follows the other letters
disrupted letters are thrown out of order
briefly cuts off the last letter

parts.note: a pier is a landing stage, a dock

explanation.surface: Someone making money at the docks after a court case is briefly interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: COURT cut short gives COUR, rearranged as CROU.
explanation.definitionFit: A croupier at a casino table rakes in the gamblers' chips.

clue.text: Conservative leading referendum vote that's split

indicators.note: leading puts this letter at the front

parts.note: Leave was a vote in the UK's 2016 EU referendum

explanation.surface: A Conservative heading the Leave campaign, a vote that divided the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Leave was one of the two options in the UK's 2016 Brexit referendum.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave is to split apart, as with a cleaver.

clue.text: Lie around snorting cocaine in ostentatious display

indicators.note: snorting takes the drug inside
turned around means read the other way

parts.note: a tale is a lie, a fib
C is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: Someone lounging around snorting cocaine in a showy display of excess.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliant show or conspicuous success, a flamboyant flourish.

clue.text: Not following rules? PM Sunak silent or worried?

indicators.note: worried means fretted over, so the letters are disturbed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is Prime Minister Rishi Sunak breaking the rules by staying silent, or merely anxious?
explanation.definitionFit: Unsportsmanlike behaviour breaks the fair-play code of sport.

clue.text: In ecstasy tablet, rat poison extremely reckless

parts.note: an E is an ecstasy tablet

indicators.note: reckless means wild, so the letters are scrambled
extremely takes the outermost letters

parts.note: outer letters P and N

explanation.surface: An ecstasy pill turns out to be rat poison, a reckless gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In ecstasy' reads as a drug reference, but it is the definition; the tablet supplies the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrapt means enraptured, carried away with delight.

clue.text: Let conservationists put grass outside

indicators.note: putting the grass outside wraps it around the other letters

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
NT is the National Trust, a British conservation charity

explanation.surface: Conservationists who let a site have it surrounded by grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Rented means let out for payment, as a flat.
